correctness.rationale: The frozen proof does not establish the upper bound: an overlap of length greater than four need not equate the last four letters of the first string to the first four of the second (e.g. 011001 -> 110011 has overlap five with different boundary four-mers). Repaired RESULT.md establishes the missing invariant for all reachable states. Starting substring-free, any newly contained third word would have to cross both copy boundaries at a maximum-overlap merge and give a strictly longer overlap, impossible. The reverse containment would imply a previous containment. An overlap from or to the new component longer than the corresponding terminal or initial copy would also give a previous containment; shorter overlaps already occurred with the original copy. Hence the maximum never increases from its initial bound of three, and original endpoint four-mers indeed determine every overlap. The state DP takes every ordered maximum-overlap merge, with no omissions at zero, and combines bitsets of additional savings; the head and tail labels remain unique across disjoint components. The independently written `python3 /workspace/repairs/2/spectrum_replay.py 16 <frozen witnesses.txt>` ran to completion, caching 2,262,415 states including 208 terminals versus the frozen C++ count of 2,262,207 nonterminals. It returned exactly savings 37..45 and replayed nine literal histories against every then-current ordered-pair overlap, checking coverage and each length 19..27. A word of length L has at most L-3 four-windows, so the replayed length-19 witness is optimal. Frozen C++ and Python programs and recorded outputs were inspected, not executed. The repaired claim has the same exact spectrum; this is not a pass for the frozen proof.

Exact extrema alone could hide holes. The gapless spectrum with literal legal histories gives a reproducible fixed-input benchmark for comparing tie rules, without advancing a universal ratio claim.
